# Spring Boot

**3.5.6 on Java 21**, via `spring-boot-starter-parent`. Three separate backends in
`Information-Systems-Modelling` — labs 2, 3 and 4 — each a forward copy of the last, all sharing the
package `pl.edu.pwr.tkubik.ism` and the same artifactId. It is the only Java web framework in the
source set.

## Starters actually used, lab by lab

| Starter / dependency | lab 2 | lab 3 | lab 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spring-boot-starter-web` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `spring-boot-starter-data-jpa` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `springdoc-openapi-starter-webmvc-ui` | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
| `build-helper-maven-plugin` | | ✓ | ✓ |
| `spring-boot-starter-aop` | | | ✓ |
| `spring-boot-starter-validation` | | | ✓ |
| `spring-boot-starter-actuator` | | | ✓ |
| `spring-security-crypto` (BCrypt only) | | | ✓ |
| jjwt 0.12.6 | | | ✓ |
| database | SQLite | [[h2-database]] | [[h2-database]] |

The additive shape of that table *is* [[forward-copy-lab-progression]]: nothing is ever removed, each
lab adds a row.

⚠ Note the two blank cells that a reader would not expect: **lab 3 has neither jjwt nor
`spring-security-crypto`**, despite its README and its OpenAPI contract both promising JWT auth with
bcrypt. See [[stateless-jwt-authentication]] for the verified detail.

## Which Spring features carry weight

- **Generated controllers.** `openapi-generator-maven-plugin` 7.20.0 emits the API interfaces from
  the OpenAPI document with `interfaceOnly` + `delegatePattern`; the hand-written controllers
  implement them. See [[contract-first-api-design]] and [[maven]].
- **AOP as the extension point.** Because the controllers implement generated interfaces, lab 4 puts
  logging, timing, audit and usage counting into aspects rather than into the controllers — see
  [[aspect-oriented-programming]].
- **RFC 9457 `ProblemDetail`.** A `@RestControllerAdvice` converts unhandled exceptions into
  structured error bodies specifically so stack traces do not reach clients.
- **Profiles.** `application.properties` (dev) and `application-prod.properties` (prod) differ in
  more than credentials: the H2 console is disabled in prod, upload limits are tightened, and a
  fully commented-out PostgreSQL/HikariCP/Flyway block sits in the prod file as a migration sketch.
- **Actuator**, dev seed data and file uploads round out lab 4.

**Security is deliberately *not* a starter.** No `spring-boot-starter-security`, no
`SecurityFilterChain`; lab 4's authentication is a hand-rolled Spring MVC interceptor over jjwt with
BCrypt borrowed from `spring-security-crypto`. See [[bcrypt-crypto-only-no-spring-security]] and
[[stateless-jwt-authentication]].

## Two documented contradictions

1. The root README says lab 4 returns **RFC-7807** `ProblemDetail`; `GlobalExceptionHandler`'s own
   javadoc says **RFC 9457**, which obsoletes 7807. The code is right.
2. The root README caps uploads at "20 MB/file and 50 files/build" — true in dev, but
   `application-prod.properties` tightens to 10 MB / 30 MB, *below* `MediaController`'s own
   constants, and the README never mentions prod.

Both are [[documentation-drift]].

## What is not proven

Three of the five Java test files assert only `contextLoads()`. Nothing tests a service
implementation, an aspect, the exception handler, the upload limits or the JWT path beyond one
end-to-end MockMvc flow. Spring Boot's testing support is present and essentially unused.

- **TODO:** no deployment, no CI, no container image, no `Dockerfile` anywhere. The prod profile
  exists but there is no evidence it was ever run. `confidence: low` on any production claim.
